name: FFmpeg Alphaextract Mask Reuse
use_when: A transparent source already contains a useful alpha plane that needs inspection, storage, modification, or reuse.
The agent needs to debug whether an overlay is truly transparent.
A mask from one layer should be applied to a different foreground layer.
avoid_when: The source has no alpha channel.
A generated grayscale mask is simpler and more controllable.
The workflow only needs a final opaque composite and no alpha debugging.
The source alpha is noisy or unapproved for reuse.

timeline_pattern.debug_rule: Use alphaextract as a diagnostic tool before rewriting a composition that appears to lose transparency.
timeline_pattern.reuse_rule: Preserve source references when an extracted mask controls a new foreground.

motion.rule: Extracted masks inherit source timing; retime or trim carefully before applying them to new foregrounds.

keyframe_values.alignment: Match extracted mask frame range to the new foreground before alphamerge.
keyframe_values.preview: Render grayscale mask previews at critical frames.
keyframe_values.trim: Trim dead mask regions that would keep invisible or unwanted alpha active.

sound.rule: No direct sound rule; preserve SFX cue markers separately if the alpha source came from a sound-synced overlay.

captions.rule: If the alpha source contains text, do not reuse its mask for unrelated caption text without checking line shape and timing.

color.rule: Extracted alpha should be inspected for feather/edge noise that could create halos when applied to new colors.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use [source_with_alpha]alphaextract[mask], preview [mask], then use [new_foreground][mask]alphamerge[masked_foreground] when reusing it.
implementation.remotion: If importing the original alpha clip, use OffthreadVideo transparent; if reusing only the matte, import the extracted mask as an image/video mask source.
implementation.blender: Use the extracted alpha as a compositor matte or material alpha input.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Export or reuse a prepared alpha/matte asset where supported; otherwise recreate the mask with CapCut masking tools.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use a matte clip as a track matte for a new foreground layer and verify alpha interpretation.

common_mistakes: Running alphaextract on opaque footage and assuming the blank result is a usable mask.
Reusing a mask with mismatched timing or dimensions.
Applying a noisy extracted matte to high-contrast text without edge cleanup.
Forgetting that extracted alpha may represent old text shapes, not the new word.
Discarding source metadata needed to regenerate the original mask.
qc: Extracted mask is visible as expected in grayscale preview.
Mask dimensions, fps, duration, and timing match the new foreground.
Edges remain clean after applying the mask to new colors or glow.
The source alpha file and reuse purpose are documented.
Final composite has no halo, chatter, or unintended transparent holes.
